category: IIS cmd.exe directory traversal exploitation (Code Red / Nimda)
evidence: Multiple distinct source IPs attempted Unicode/double-encoded directory-traversal payloads targeting /scripts/..%5c../winnt/system32/cmd.exe, /scripts/.%252e/.%252e/winnt/system32/cmd.exe, /scripts/..%c0%af../..%c0%af../..%c0%af../winnt/system32/cmd.exe, and /scripts/..%e0%80%af../..%e0%80%af../..%e0%80%af../winnt/system32/cmd.exe with the query string '?/c+dir'. These are classic Code Red / Nimda worm signatures actively attempting remote command execution against an IIS unicode-decoding vulnerability (CVE-2000-0884). The payloads are crafted with multiple encoding tricks to bypass input-validation filters.
sample_entry: [Fri Jun 10 01:23:50 2005] [error] [client 63.203.254.140] Invalid method in request get /scripts/.%252e/.%252e/winnt/system32/cmd.exe?/c+dir

evidence: Client 202.118.167.71 made multiple repeated requests for /scripts/root.exe?/c+dir across Jun 11, Jun 14, and Jun 15. root.exe is the well-known backdoor left by the Code Red II / Nimda worms on compromised IIS servers; invoking it with '?/c+dir' is an active attempt to execute arbitrary commands via the existing backdoor. This is exploitation, not mere scanning.
sample_entry: [Sat Jun 11 12:00:08 2005] [error] [client 202.118.167.71] Invalid method in request get /scripts/root.exe?/c+dir

evidence: Multiple source IPs from a /24-range (210.22.201.x) and other hosts issued the canonical Nimda/Code-Red-II vulnerability scan sequence in rapid succession: root.exe, MSADC, c, d, scripts/..%5c.., _vti_bin, _mem_bin, msadc, and various encoded traversal payloads (..%5c.., ..%2f.., ..\xc0\xaf.., ..\xc1\x1c.., ..\xc1\x9c..). This signature matches the Nessus/IIS-auditor fingerprint for known IIS vulnerabilities (MS00-078, MS01-026, FrontPage _vti_bin exposure). One additional isolated _vti_bin scan from 66.201.171.199 is also present.

Client 202.133.98.6 issued hundreds of requests in a tight loop (~3:03:03 to 3:03:13) probing for awstats.pl across numerous locations (/cgi-bin/awstats, /cgi-bin/awstats.pl, /awstats/awstats.pl, /stats/awstats.pl, /cgi-bin/stats, /cgi, etc.). This is the well-known AWStats configdir / remote-command-execution probe (CVE-2005-0116, CVE-2005-1527) targeting the awstats.pl CGI. The volume and structured path-enumeration indicate an automated scanner rather than manual probing.
sample_entry: [Sat Jun 11 03:03:03 2005] [error] [client 202.133.98.6] script not found or unable to stat: /var/www/cgi-bin/awstats

evidence: Multiple clients repeatedly probed /var/www/html/_vti_bin, sometimes accompanied by 'URI too long (longer than 8190)' errors and oversized requests. _vti_bin is the FrontPage Server Extensions / SharePoint endpoint, historically vulnerable to information disclosure and buffer-overflow issues (e.g., MS03-051). Repeated probing plus oversized URIs suggests automated tools attempting FrontPage exploit paths.

Client 212.238.198.203 issued 20+ rapid requests for /var/www/cgi-bin/openwebmail over ~10 seconds. OpenWebMail has multiple known remote-command-execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2003-0292, CVE-2004-0107). The pattern is consistent with automated exploit-tool scanning.

category: Repeated 'sumthin' reconnaissance probe from single IPs
evidence: Clients issued 15-25 identical requests for /sumthin within a single second (e.g., 81.199.21.119 at 19:23:31-19:23:32 with 21 hits; 194.116.250.2 at 03:37:39-03:37:42 with 23 hits). The 'sumthin' probe is the signature of automated reconnaissance/scanning tools (notably 'Stealth' and similar scanners) fingerprinting servers before follow-on attacks. High request rate from one IP strongly indicates scanning rather than normal user behaviour.

category: Repeated directory-index probing (forbidden) from single IPs
evidence: Multiple source IPs generated bursts (10-20+ hits each) of 'Directory index forbidden by rule: /var/www/html/' within seconds, indicating automated probing for open directory listings, default content, or vulnerable applications. Examples: 195.23.79.241 produced ~19 hits in one second on Jun 13 18:38:25; 60.191.134.226 produced 19 hits Jun 14 13:17:00-13:17:07. Repeated forbidden responses from a single IP are reconnaissance, not normal browsing.

evidence: Numerous 'jk2_init() Can't find child N in scoreboard' and 'mod_jk child init 1 -2' errors occur during/after restarts and during the awstats scan. These reflect a misconfigured mod_jk2 worker setup (workers2.properties), not active attacks. Severity is low because mod_jk2 is end-of-life and the errors are administrative/configuration noise.
sample_entry: [Sun Jun 12 04:04:33 2005] [error] jk2_init() Can't find child 8728 in scoreboard

evidence: Repeated '[notice] LDAP: SSL support unavailable' messages at each Apache start. This is informational and indicates LDAP was built without SSL/TLS support; on a properly hardened server this is suboptimal but not itself evidence of an attack.

'request failed: URI too long (longer than 8190)' errors. These come from the same IPs conducting _vti_bin scanning, so they are part of broader reconnaissance, but individually they are typically benign client misbehaviour. Listed as low because by themselves they indicate only client-side bugs or oversize probes without successful exploitation.
